doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Being scared playing with great musicians
summary: Butch says he is almost constantly afraid of embarrassing himself around giants, mainly of losing the tempo.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: I was kind of wondering about that, like night after night the band chooses Freddie. You know you said in our first interview that when you joined Basie you were young and foolish and scared to death. So I’m wondering if there were other times in your career, before or after Basie, that you found yourself in the situation that you were scared to death?

Pretty much constantly. Whenever I’ve been in contact with great musicians, magnificent giants, I’ve always, you know, secretly prayed that I wasn’t going to make a fool of myself. If nothing else at least I was going to keep the tempo, which is not an easy thing to do sometimes, especially if you’re playing long charts, you know, things that go on for seven, eight, nine, ten minutes. But I have been scared out of my gourd many-a-time.
